clues.clue: Sworn in 2021 as New York's first woman governor, this Buffalo Democrat leads the state's executive branch.
clues.reveal: Kathy Hochul. New York's first woman governor, who took office in 2021 after serving as lieutenant governor.

clues.clue: The governor can reject a bill passed by the Legislature using this power.
clues.reveal: Veto. The governor may veto legislation, which the Legislature can override with a two-thirds vote of each house.

clues.clue: First in the line of succession to the governor, this separately elected official is Antonio Delgado as of 2026.
clues.reveal: Lieutenant Governor. Antonio Delgado holds the office as of 2026; the Lt. Governor presides over the State Senate and is first in succession.

clues.clue: New York's legislature has two chambers: the State Senate and this larger lower house.
clues.reveal: Assembly. The 150-member State Assembly is the lower house; the 63-member Senate is the upper house.

clues.clue: This Bronx Democrat, Carl Heastie, holds the most powerful post in the Assembly.
clues.reveal: Speaker. Carl Heastie of the Bronx is Speaker of the Assembly, the chamber's top leader.

clues.clue: Andrea Stewart-Cousins leads the State Senate with this title, the first woman to hold it.
clues.reveal: Majority Leader. Andrea Stewart-Cousins is Senate Majority Leader and Temporary President, the first woman to lead a legislative chamber in Albany.

clues.clue: The state's annual spending plan, due by April 1, is known by this name.
clues.reveal: Budget. The state budget is due April 1; late budgets are common when the governor and legislative leaders disagree.
clues.app_title: State budget tracker on the app

clues.clue: The capital city where the Legislature meets, on the Hudson River, is this.
clues.reveal: Albany. New York's capital since 1797, where the Legislature and governor's offices sit.

clues.clue: The closed-door budget deals among the governor and two legislative leaders are nicknamed this, for the room's powerful occupants.
clues.reveal: Three Men in a Room. The phrase for New York's tradition of the governor and two legislative leaders cutting budget deals privately.

clues.clue: The state's chief legal officer, Letitia James as of 2026, holds this elected office.
clues.reveal: Attorney General. Letitia 'Tish' James is New York's elected chief legal officer.

clues.clue: The state's chief fiscal officer and auditor, Tom DiNapoli, holds this elected statewide office.
clues.reveal: Comptroller. Thomas DiNapoli is New York's elected Comptroller, auditing state finances and managing the pension fund.

clues.clue: New York's highest court has this name, unusual because in most states it refers to a trial court.
clues.reveal: Court of Appeals. New York's highest court; confusingly, the state's trial court is called the Supreme Court.
